classification.habitat: Moist shady evergreen forests and cultivated in humid areas.
classification.distribution: Hotter parts of India from the central Himalaya to Assam, lower hills of West Bengal and evergreen forests of the Western Ghats; cultivated in North-East and South India.

identification.description: Cylindrical dark fruit spikes formed by fused berries, characteristically aromatic and pungent.
identification.whole_plant: Slender, aromatic, creeping or climbing undershrub with perennial woody roots and jointed stems.
identification.root: Perennial, woody, cylindrical roots and root-stock, used as Pippalimula; pungent.
identification.stem: Slender, jointed, creeping or climbing stems, swollen at nodes and rooting there.
identification.leaf: Simple, alternate; lower leaves broadly ovate-cordate and petiolate, upper ones oblong and nearly sessile; 5–9 nerved.
identification.flower: Unisexual flowers in dense cylindrical spikes; male spikes slender and long, female spikes shorter and thicker.
identification.fruit: Catkin-like fruit greenish-black to black, cylindrical, 2.5–5 cm long and 0.4–1 cm thick, made of minute sessile fruitlets around an axis; taste pungent causing numbness, odour aromatic.
identification.seed: Minute seeds embedded singly in the fused berries.
identification_points: Rough surface of many minute fused fruitlets
Cross section shows central axis with 6–12 fruitlets
Pungent taste causing numbness of the tongue

therapeutics.anupana: Madhu (honey) in Kasa and Shwasa; Ksheera (milk) in Vardhamana Pippali Rasayana
therapeutics.precautions: Prolonged or excessive use is cautioned in classics (Charaka advises against continuous use except as Rasayana); it may aggravate Pitta in high doses.
therapeutics.contraindications: Amlapitta, Raktapitta and other Pitta-predominant states; caution in pregnancy in medicinal doses; piperine may raise blood levels of some medicines.

shlokas:
पिप्पली मागधी कृष्णा वैदेही चपला कणा ।
उपकुल्योषणा शौण्डी कोला स्यात्तीक्ष्णतण्डुला ॥
पिप्पली दीपनी वृष्या स्वादुपाका रसायनी ।
अनुष्णा कटुका स्निग्धा वातश्लेष्महरी लघुः ॥
पिप्पली रेचनी हन्ति श्वासकासोदरज्वरान् ।
कुष्ठप्रमेहगुल्मार्शःप्लीहशूलाममारुतान् ॥
nighantu_references: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu, Haritakyadi Varga, Pippali passage (often numbered 50–51 in searchable recensions; other editions differ).

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: API lists essential oil and alkaloids; piperine and piperlongumine are the principal amide alkaloids.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Long pepper is a powerful stimulant for the digestive and respiratory systems. It is a key ingredient in the Trikatu formula.
recognized_uses: Respiratory and digestive stimulant in traditional systems
modern_information.safety_notes: Generally safe in the stated dose; piperine may alter the metabolism of co-administered drugs.

exam_points: Pippali = Piper longum L., family Piperaceae
Useful part: dried fruit (spike); root is Pippalimula
Rasa Katu; Guna Laghu, Snigdha, Tikshna; Virya Anushnasheeta; Vipaka Madhura
Karma: Deepana, Rasayana, Vrishya, Kasa-Shwasahara, Pleehahara
Vardhamana Pippali Rasayana: dose increased and decreased daily
Member of Trikatu and Chaturushana (with Pippalimula)
viva_questions: What is the difference between Trikatu and Chaturushana?
student.quick_revision: Pippali (Piper longum): dried fruit, root as Pippalimula; Katu rasa, Laghu-Snigdha-Tikshna guna, Anushna-sheeta virya, Madhura vipaka; Kapha-Vata shamaka; Dipana, Rasayana; one of the Trikatu.

teaching_points: Pippali as a Katu drug with Madhura Vipaka and Rasayana action.
practical_points: Cut a spike transversely and count fruitlets.

doctor.quick_reference: Pippali (Piper longum fruit): Katu, Madhura Vipaka, Anushnasheeta; Rasayana, Deepana; for Kasa, Shwasa, Pleeha, Jwara; 1–3 g with honey.
doctor.anupana: Madhu (honey) in Kasa and Shwasa; Ksheera (milk) in Vardhamana Pippali Rasayana
key_precautions: Avoid prolonged continuous use outside Rasayana protocol
